title: Ueber das Zustandekommen der Diphtherie-Immunität und der Tetanus-Immunität bei Thieren
authors: Behring E, Kitasato S
summary: Showed that serum from immunized animals transfers protection against diphtheria and tetanus toxins, founding antitoxin serum therapy and the concept of antibodies as therapeutics.

title: The internal secretion of the pancreas
authors: Banting FG, Best CH
venue: Journal of Laboratory and Clinical Medicine 7:251–266
summary: Isolation of pancreatic extracts (insulin) that lowered blood glucose in diabetic dogs, leading to the first protein hormone therapy.

title: Continuous cultures of fused cells secreting antibody of predefined specificity
authors: Köhler G, Milstein C
summary: Invented hybridoma technology for producing monoclonal antibodies of a single defined specificity, the foundation of antibody therapeutics and immunodiagnostics.

title: Expression in Escherichia coli of a chemically synthesized gene for the hormone somatostatin
authors: Itakura K, Hirose T, Crea R, Riggs AD, Heyneker HL, Bolivar F, et al.
summary: First expression of a chemically synthesized human peptide hormone gene in bacteria, proving recombinant production of human proteins was feasible.

title: Expression in Escherichia coli of chemically synthesized genes for human insulin
authors: Goeddel DV, Kleid DG, Bolivar F, Heyneker HL, Yansura DG, Crea R, et al.
summary: Genentech's recombinant production of human insulin A and B chains in E. coli, leading to Humulin (1982), the first approved recombinant drug and the start of the biotech industry.

title: Direct expression in Escherichia coli of a DNA sequence coding for human growth hormone
authors: Goeddel DV, Heyneker HL, Hozumi T, Arentzen R, Itakura K, Yansura DG, et al.
summary: Recombinant human growth hormone produced in bacteria, which replaced cadaver-derived hGH after prion contamination was discovered.

title: Hybrid hybridomas and their use in immunohistochemistry
authors: Milstein C, Cuello AC
summary: Fused two hybridomas ('quadromas') to produce bispecific antibodies, the conceptual origin of bispecific antibody therapeutics.

title: Chimeric human antibody molecules: mouse antigen-binding domains with human constant region domains
authors: Morrison SL, Johnson MJ, Herzenberg LA, Oi VT
summary: Engineered mouse-human chimeric antibodies to reduce immunogenicity, the format later used by rituximab and infliximab.

title: Cloning and expression of the human erythropoietin gene
authors: Lin FK, Suggs S, Lin CH, Browne JK, Smalling R, Egrie JC, et al.
summary: Amgen's cloning and mammalian-cell expression of human EPO, yielding epoetin alfa, one of the most commercially successful early biologics.

title: Replacing the complementarity-determining regions in a human antibody with those from a mouse
authors: Jones PT, Dear PH, Foote J, Neuberger MS, Winter G
summary: Introduced CDR grafting to humanize antibodies, enabling a generation of therapeutics such as trastuzumab and many others.

title: Phage antibodies: filamentous phage displaying antibody variable domains
authors: McCafferty J, Griffiths AD, Winter G, Chiswell DJ
summary: Displayed antibody fragments on filamentous phage, enabling in vitro selection of fully human antibodies (e.g. adalimumab).

title: Randomised double-blind comparison of chimeric monoclonal antibody to tumour necrosis factor alpha (cA2) versus placebo in rheumatoid arthritis
authors: Elliott MJ, Maini RN, Feldmann M, Kalden JR, Antoni C, Smolen JS, et al.
summary: Controlled trial showing anti-TNF antibody (infliximab) treats rheumatoid arthritis, validating cytokine blockade and launching the anti-TNF biologic class.

title: Rituximab chimeric anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody therapy for relapsed indolent lymphoma: half of patients respond to a four-dose treatment program
authors: McLaughlin P, Grillo-López AJ, Link BK, Levy R, Czuczman MS, Williams ME, et al.
summary: Pivotal trial of rituximab, the first monoclonal antibody approved for cancer (1997), transforming lymphoma treatment.

title: Use of chemotherapy plus a monoclonal antibody against HER2 for metastatic breast cancer that overexpresses HER2
authors: Slamon DJ, Leyland-Jones B, Shak S, Fuchs H, Paton V, Bajamonde A, et al.
summary: Phase 3 trial showing humanized anti-HER2 trastuzumab improves survival, a landmark for biomarker-targeted antibody therapy.

title: Approval of adalimumab (Humira), the first fully human therapeutic monoclonal antibody
authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Abbott Laboratories
summary: Adalimumab, derived by phage display, became the first fully human mAb approved and later the world's best-selling drug.

title: Development of potent monoclonal antibody auristatin conjugates for cancer therapy
authors: Doronina SO, Toki BE, Torgov MY, Mendelsohn BA, Cerveny CG, Chace DF, et al.
summary: Developed MMAE auristatin linker-payload chemistry that underpins many antibody-drug conjugates, including brentuximab vedotin.

title: Tumor regression in cancer patients by very low doses of a T cell-engaging antibody
authors: Bargou R, Leo E, Zugmaier G, Klinger M, Goebeler M, Knop S, et al.
summary: Clinical proof that the CD19xCD3 bispecific T-cell engager blinatumomab redirects T cells to kill lymphoma, establishing the BiTE class.

title: Trastuzumab emtansine for HER2-positive advanced breast cancer
authors: Verma S, Miles D, Gianni L, Krop IE, Welslau M, Baselga J, et al.
summary: EMILIA trial establishing T-DM1, an antibody-drug conjugate, as superior to standard therapy in HER2+ breast cancer.

title: Isolation and characterization of exendin-4, an exendin-3 analogue, from Heloderma suspectum venom
authors: Eng J, Kleinman WA, Singh L, Singh G, Raufman JP
summary: Discovered exendin-4 in Gila monster venom, a long-acting GLP-1 receptor agonist that became exenatide, the first GLP-1 drug.

title: Once-weekly semaglutide in adults with overweight or obesity
authors: Wilding JPH, Batterham RL, Calanna S, Davies M, Van Gaal LF, Lingvay I, et al.
summary: STEP 1 trial showing ~15% weight loss with semaglutide, launching the GLP-1 obesity drug era.

title: Trastuzumab deruxtecan in previously treated HER2-low advanced breast cancer
authors: Modi S, Jacot W, Yamashita T, Sohn J, Vidal M, Tokunaga E, et al.
summary: DESTINY-Breast04 showed a next-generation ADC benefits HER2-low tumors, redefining a new targetable breast cancer population.

title: Lecanemab in early Alzheimer's disease
authors: van Dyck CH, Swanson CJ, Aisen P, Bateman RJ, Chen C, Gee M, et al.
summary: CLARITY AD trial: an anti-amyloid protofibril antibody modestly slowed cognitive decline, leading to full approval of the first disease-modifying Alzheimer's antibody.

title: An Inquiry into the Causes and Effects of the Variolae Vaccinae
authors: Jenner E
summary: Described cowpox inoculation protecting against smallpox, founding vaccination.

title: Compte rendu sommaire des expériences faites à Pouilly-le-Fort, près de Melun, sur la vaccination charbonneuse
authors: Pasteur L, Chamberland C, Roux E
venue: Comptes Rendus de l'Académie des Sciences 92
summary: Public demonstration of an attenuated anthrax vaccine in sheep, generalizing vaccination to laboratory-attenuated pathogens.

title: Cultivation of the Lansing strain of poliomyelitis virus in cultures of various human embryonic tissues
authors: Enders JF, Weller TH, Robbins FC
summary: Grew poliovirus in non-neural tissue culture, enabling mass production of viral vaccines (Nobel 1954).

title: Studies in human subjects on active immunization against poliomyelitis. I. A preliminary report of experiments in progress
authors: Salk JE
summary: First human results with formalin-inactivated poliovirus vaccine, leading to the 1954 field trial and 1955 licensure.

title: Oral poliovirus vaccine (Sabin strains) licensed in the United States
authors: Sabin AB
summary: Live attenuated oral polio vaccine providing mucosal immunity and easy mass administration, the workhorse of global polio eradication.

title: Preparation, characterization, and immunogenicity of Haemophilus influenzae type b polysaccharide-protein conjugates
authors: Schneerson R, Barrera O, Sutton A, Robbins JB
summary: Conjugating capsular polysaccharide to a carrier protein made it immunogenic in infants, the basis of Hib, pneumococcal and meningococcal conjugate vaccines.

title: Synthesis and assembly of hepatitis B virus surface antigen particles in yeast
authors: Valenzuela P, Medina A, Rutter WJ, Ammerer G, Hall BD
summary: Yeast-expressed HBsAg self-assembled into particles, leading to the first recombinant vaccine (hepatitis B, licensed 1986).

title: Papillomavirus L1 major capsid protein self-assembles into virus-like particles that are highly immunogenic
authors: Kirnbauer R, Booy F, Cheng N, Lowy DR, Schiller JT
summary: Showed recombinant L1 forms highly immunogenic virus-like particles, the basis of HPV vaccines.

title: Quadrivalent vaccine against human papillomavirus to prevent high-grade cervical lesions
authors: FUTURE II Study Group
summary: Phase 3 efficacy of the quadrivalent HPV VLP vaccine (Gardasil) against cervical precancer, enabling cervical cancer prevention by vaccination.

title: Structure-based design of a fusion glycoprotein vaccine for respiratory syncytial virus
authors: McLellan JS, Chen M, Joyce MG, Sastry M, Stewart-Jones GBE, Yang Y, et al.
summary: Stabilized RSV F in its prefusion conformation (DS-Cav1), demonstrating structure-based vaccine design and paving the way for RSV vaccines.

title: Immunogenicity and structures of a rationally designed prefusion MERS-CoV spike antigen
authors: Pallesen J, Wang N, Corbett KS, Wrapp D, Kirchdoerfer RN, Turner HL, et al.
summary: Introduced the two-proline (2P) prefusion-stabilizing mutations in coronavirus spikes, used in most COVID-19 vaccines.

title: An mRNA vaccine against SARS-CoV-2 — preliminary report
authors: Jackson LA, Anderson EJ, Rouphael NG, Roberts PC, Makhene M, Coler RN, et al.
summary: First-in-human phase 1 results for mRNA-1273, showing robust neutralizing responses within months of the viral sequence release.

title: Safety and efficacy of the BNT162b2 mRNA Covid-19 vaccine
authors: Polack FP, Thomas SJ, Kitchin N, Absalon J, Gurtman A, Lockhart S, et al.
summary: Phase 3 trial showing 95% efficacy of the Pfizer-BioNTech nucleoside-modified mRNA-LNP vaccine; first mRNA product ever authorized.

title: Efficacy and safety of the mRNA-1273 SARS-CoV-2 vaccine
authors: Baden LR, El Sahly HM, Essink B, Kotloff K, Frey S, Novak R, et al.
summary: COVE phase 3 trial showing 94.1% efficacy of Moderna's mRNA-1273, confirming the mRNA vaccine platform.

title: Respiratory syncytial virus prefusion F protein vaccine in older adults
authors: Papi A, Ison MG, Langley JM, Lee DG, Leroux-Roels I, Martinon-Torres F, et al.
summary: AReSVi-006 trial of an adjuvanted prefusion-F vaccine, leading to the first approved RSV vaccines in 2023.

title: Safety and efficacy of malaria vaccine candidate R21/Matrix-M in African children: a multicentre, double-blind, randomised, phase 3 trial
authors: Datoo MS, Dicko A, Tinto H, Ouédraogo JB, Hamaluba M, Olotu A, et al.
summary: Phase 3 results for R21/Matrix-M, a circumsporozoite-HBsAg VLP malaria vaccine recommended by WHO for children.

title: T lymphocyte-directed gene therapy for ADA- SCID: initial trial results after 4 years
authors: Blaese RM, Culver KW, Miller AD, Carter CS, Fleisher T, Clerici M, et al.
summary: Report of the first approved human gene therapy trial (begun 1990 with Ashanti DeSilva), using retrovirally transduced T cells to treat ADA deficiency.

title: In vivo gene delivery and stable transduction of nondividing cells by a lentiviral vector
authors: Naldini L, Blömer U, Gallay P, Ory D, Mulligan R, Gage FH, et al.
summary: Developed HIV-derived lentiviral vectors that transduce non-dividing cells, now standard for ex vivo HSC gene therapy and CAR-T manufacturing.

title: Gene therapy of human severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID)-X1 disease
authors: Cavazzana-Calvo M, Hacein-Bey S, de Saint Basile G, Gross F, Yvon E, Nusbaum P, et al.
summary: First clear clinical success of gene therapy: retrovirally corrected stem cells restored immunity in X-SCID infants.

title: Novel adeno-associated viruses from rhesus monkeys as vectors for human gene therapy
authors: Gao GP, Alvira MR, Wang L, Calcedo R, Johnston J, Wilson JM
summary: Discovered AAV7 and AAV8 serotypes with improved tissue tropism, expanding the AAV vector toolkit used in liver and muscle gene therapies.

title: Fatal systemic inflammatory response syndrome in a ornithine transcarbamylase deficient patient following adenoviral gene transfer
authors: Raper SE, Chirmule N, Lee FS, Wivel NA, Bagg A, Gao GP, et al.
summary: Analysis of the 1999 death of Jesse Gelsinger after adenoviral vector infusion, which reshaped gene therapy safety oversight.

title: LMO2-associated clonal T cell proliferation in two patients after gene therapy for SCID-X1
authors: Hacein-Bey-Abina S, von Kalle C, Schmidt M, McCormack MP, Wulffraat N, Leboulch P, et al.
summary: Revealed insertional oncogenesis by gamma-retroviral vectors, driving the shift to self-inactivating and lentiviral vectors.

title: Adenovirus-associated virus vector-mediated gene transfer in hemophilia B
authors: Nathwani AC, Tuddenham EGD, Rangarajan S, Rosales C, McIntosh J, Linch DC, et al.
summary: Single peripheral infusion of AAV8-factor IX produced durable expression in hemophilia B, a turning point for systemic AAV gene therapy.

title: An erythroid enhancer of BCL11A subject to genetic variation determines fetal hemoglobin level
authors: Bauer DE, Kamran SC, Lessard S, Xu J, Fujiwara Y, Lin C, et al.
summary: Identified the erythroid-specific BCL11A enhancer as a target whose disruption reactivates fetal hemoglobin, the basis of exa-cel.

title: Efficacy and safety of voretigene neparvovec (AAV2-hRPE65v2) in patients with RPE65-mediated inherited retinal dystrophy: a randomised, controlled, open-label, phase 3 trial
authors: Russell S, Bennett J, Wellman JA, Chung DC, Yu ZF, Tillman A, et al.
summary: Phase 3 trial supporting Luxturna, the first FDA-approved gene therapy for an inherited disease (2017).

title: Single-dose gene-replacement therapy for spinal muscular atrophy
authors: Mendell JR, Al-Zaidy S, Shell R, Arnold WD, Rodino-Klapac LR, Prior TW, et al.
summary: Intravenous AAV9-SMN1 dramatically improved survival in SMA type 1 infants, leading to Zolgensma approval (2019).

title: CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing for sickle cell disease and β-thalassemia
authors: Frangoul H, Altshuler D, Cappellini MD, Chen YS, Domm J, Eustace BK, et al.
summary: First patients treated with CRISPR-edited autologous stem cells disrupting the BCL11A enhancer (exa-cel), eliminating crises and transfusion dependence.

title: CRISPR-Cas9 in vivo gene editing for transthyretin amyloidosis
authors: Gillmore JD, Gane E, Taubel J, Kao J, Fontana M, Maitland ML, et al.
summary: First systemic in vivo CRISPR editing in humans: LNP-delivered NTLA-2001 knocked out TTR in the liver.

title: In vivo CRISPR base editing of PCSK9 durably lowers cholesterol in primates
authors: Musunuru K, Chadwick AC, Mizoguchi T, Garcia SP, DeNizio JE, Reiss CW, et al.
summary: LNP-delivered adenine base editor durably knocked down PCSK9 in monkeys, enabling in vivo base-editing therapies.

title: Approval of Casgevy (exagamglogene autotemcel), the first CRISPR-based therapy
authors: UK MHRA; US Food and Drug Administration; Vertex Pharmaceuticals; CRISPR Therapeutics
venue: UK MHRA approval (Nov 2023) and US FDA approval (Dec 2023)
summary: First regulatory approvals of a CRISPR genome-editing medicine, for sickle cell disease and transfusion-dependent β-thalassemia.

title: Patient-specific in vivo gene editing to cure a rare genetic disease
authors: Musunuru K, Grandinette SA, Wang X, et al.
summary: A bespoke LNP-delivered base editor designed and dosed within months to treat infant KJ with CPS1 deficiency, the first personalized in vivo gene-editing therapy.

title: Intravenous infusion of bone marrow in patients receiving radiation and chemotherapy
authors: Thomas ED, Lochte HL Jr, Lu WC, Ferrebee JW
summary: Early human bone marrow infusion studies that founded hematopoietic stem cell transplantation, the first cell therapy (Nobel 1990).

title: Establishment in culture of pluripotential cells from mouse embryos
authors: Evans MJ, Kaufman MH
summary: Derived mouse embryonic stem cells, enabling gene targeting and the field of pluripotent stem cell biology.

title: Isolation of a pluripotent cell line from early mouse embryos cultured in medium conditioned by teratocarcinoma stem cells
authors: Martin GR
summary: Independent derivation of mouse ES cells; coined the term 'embryonic stem cell'.

title: Viable offspring derived from fetal and adult mammalian cells
authors: Wilmut I, Schnieke AE, McWhir J, Kind AJ, Campbell KHS
summary: Cloning of Dolly the sheep by somatic cell nuclear transfer, proving adult nuclei can be reprogrammed to totipotency.

title: Embryonic stem cell lines derived from human blastocysts
authors: Thomson JA, Itskovitz-Eldor J, Shapiro SS, Waknitz MA, Swiergiel JJ, Marshall VS, et al.
summary: First human embryonic stem cell lines, opening human regenerative medicine and disease modeling.

title: Islet transplantation in seven patients with type 1 diabetes mellitus using a glucocorticoid-free immunosuppressive regimen
authors: Shapiro AMJ, Lakey JRT, Ryan EA, Korbutt GS, Toth E, Warnock GL, et al.
summary: The Edmonton protocol achieved insulin independence via donor islet infusion, proving cell replacement could treat type 1 diabetes.

title: Induction of pluripotent stem cells from mouse embryonic and adult fibroblast cultures by defined factors
authors: Takahashi K, Yamanaka S
summary: Four transcription factors (Oct4, Sox2, Klf4, c-Myc) reprogram fibroblasts into induced pluripotent stem cells (Nobel 2012).

title: Induction of pluripotent stem cells from adult human fibroblasts by defined factors
authors: Takahashi K, Tanabe K, Ohnuki M, Narita M, Ichisaka T, Tomoda K, et al.
summary: Generated human iPSCs, providing patient-specific pluripotent cells without embryos.

title: Single Lgr5 stem cells build crypt-villus structures in vitro without a mesenchymal niche
authors: Sato T, Vries RG, Snippert HJ, van de Wetering M, Barker N, Stange DE, et al.
summary: Grew self-organizing intestinal organoids from single adult stem cells, launching organoid technology for disease modeling and regeneration.

title: Generation of functional human pancreatic β cells in vitro
authors: Pagliuca FW, Millman JR, Gürtler M, Segel M, Van Dervort A, Ryu JH, et al.
summary: Scalable differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into glucose-responsive beta cells, the basis of stem-cell islet therapies.

title: Autologous induced stem-cell-derived retinal cells for macular degeneration
authors: Mandai M, Watanabe A, Kurimoto Y, Hirami Y, Morinaga C, Daimon T, et al.
summary: First transplantation of iPSC-derived tissue (retinal pigment epithelium) into a patient.

title: Stem cell-derived, fully differentiated islets for type 1 diabetes
authors: Reichman TW, Markmann JF, Odorico J, et al.
summary: Phase 1/2 results for zimislecel (VX-880), stem cell-derived islets that restored endogenous insulin and produced insulin independence in most patients.

title: Phase I trial of hES cell-derived dopaminergic neurons for Parkinson's disease
authors: Tabar V, Sarva H, Lozano AM, et al.
summary: First-in-human trial of embryonic stem cell-derived dopaminergic progenitors (bemdaneprocel) showing graft survival and safety in Parkinson's disease.

title: Inhibition of Rous sarcoma virus replication and cell transformation by a specific oligodeoxynucleotide
authors: Zamecnik PC, Stephenson ML
summary: First demonstration that a synthetic antisense oligonucleotide can inhibit gene expression, founding antisense therapeutics.

title: Cationic liposome-mediated RNA transfection
authors: Malone RW, Felgner PL, Verma IM
summary: Delivered mRNA into cells with cationic lipids and observed protein expression, an early step toward lipid-delivered mRNA medicines.

title: Direct gene transfer into mouse muscle in vivo
authors: Wolff JA, Malone RW, Williams P, Chong W, Acsadi G, Jani A, et al.
summary: Showed naked mRNA and plasmid DNA injected into muscle are expressed in vivo, the conceptual origin of mRNA and DNA vaccines.

title: Potent and specific genetic interference by double-stranded RNA in Caenorhabditis elegans
authors: Fire A, Xu S, Montgomery MK, Kostas SA, Driver SE, Mello CC
summary: Discovered RNA interference triggered by double-stranded RNA (Nobel 2006).

title: Duplexes of 21-nucleotide RNAs mediate RNA interference in cultured mammalian cells
authors: Elbashir SM, Harborth J, Lendeckel W, Yalcin A, Weber K, Tuschl T
summary: Synthetic siRNAs silence genes in mammalian cells without the interferon response, enabling RNAi therapeutics.

title: Suppression of RNA recognition by Toll-like receptors: the impact of nucleoside modification and the evolutionary origin of RNA
authors: Karikó K, Buckstein M, Ni H, Weissman D
summary: Showed modified nucleosides (e.g. pseudouridine) let mRNA evade innate immune sensing, the key enabler of mRNA vaccines (Nobel 2023).

title: Incorporation of pseudouridine into mRNA yields superior nonimmunogenic vector with increased translational capacity and biological stability
authors: Karikó K, Muramatsu H, Welsh FA, Ludwig J, Kato H, Akira S, et al.
summary: Pseudouridine-modified mRNA was both less immunogenic and more efficiently translated in vivo.

title: Rational design of cationic lipids for siRNA delivery
authors: Semple SC, Akinc A, Chen J, Sandhu AP, Mui BL, Cho CK, et al.
summary: Designed ionizable lipids (DLin-KC2-DMA) for potent lipid nanoparticle delivery, the lineage leading to patisiran and mRNA vaccine LNPs.

title: Multivalent N-acetylgalactosamine-conjugated siRNA localizes in hepatocytes and elicits robust RNAi-mediated gene silencing
authors: Nair JK, Willoughby JLS, Chan A, Charisse K, Alam MR, Wang Q, et al.
venue: Journal of the American Chemical Society 136:16958–16961
summary: Triantennary GalNAc conjugates deliver subcutaneous siRNA to hepatocytes, the platform behind givosiran, inclisiran and others.

title: Nusinersen versus sham control in infantile-onset spinal muscular atrophy
authors: Finkel RS, Mercuri E, Darras BT, Connolly AM, Kuntz NL, Kirschner J, et al.
summary: ENDEAR trial of a splice-switching antisense oligonucleotide that increases SMN protein, the first approved SMA therapy.

title: Patisiran, an RNAi therapeutic, for hereditary transthyretin amyloidosis
authors: Adams D, Gonzalez-Duarte A, O'Riordan WD, Yang CC, Ueda M, Kristen AV, et al.
summary: APOLLO trial leading to patisiran, the first approved siRNA drug and first LNP-delivered RNA medicine.

title: Two phase 3 trials of inclisiran in patients with elevated LDL cholesterol
authors: Ray KK, Wright RS, Kallend D, Koenig W, Leiter LA, Raal FJ, et al.
summary: Twice-yearly GalNAc-siRNA against PCSK9 halved LDL cholesterol, bringing RNAi to common cardiovascular disease.

title: The treatment of malignant tumors by repeated inoculations of erysipelas: with a report of ten original cases
authors: Coley WB
venue: American Journal of the Medical Sciences 105:487–511
summary: Bacterial toxin injections ('Coley's toxins') induced tumor regressions, the earliest systematic cancer immunotherapy.

title: Use of tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes and interleukin-2 in the immunotherapy of patients with metastatic melanoma
authors: Rosenberg SA, Packard BS, Aebersold PM, Solomon D, Topalian SL, Toy ST, et al.
summary: Adoptive transfer of expanded tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes caused melanoma regressions, founding adoptive T-cell therapy.

title: Induced expression of PD-1, a novel member of the immunoglobulin gene superfamily, upon programmed cell death
authors: Ishida Y, Agata Y, Shibahara K, Honjo T
summary: Discovered PD-1, later shown to be an inhibitory immune checkpoint and the target of anti-PD-1 therapies (Nobel 2018).

title: Specific activation and targeting of cytotoxic lymphocytes through chimeric single chains consisting of antibody-binding domains and the gamma or zeta subunits of the immunoglobulin and T-cell receptors
authors: Eshhar Z, Waks T, Gross G, Schindler DG
summary: Created the single-chain chimeric antigen receptor (scFv fused to CD3ζ), the blueprint of CAR-T cells.

title: Enhancement of antitumor immunity by CTLA-4 blockade
authors: Leach DR, Krummel MF, Allison JP
summary: Antibody blockade of the CTLA-4 checkpoint caused tumor rejection in mice, the founding experiment of checkpoint immunotherapy (Nobel 2018).

title: Improved survival with ipilimumab in patients with metastatic melanoma
authors: Hodi FS, O'Day SJ, McDermott DF, Weber RW, Sosman JA, Haanen JB, et al.
summary: First therapy to improve overall survival in metastatic melanoma, leading to approval of the first checkpoint inhibitor.

title: Chimeric antigen receptor–modified T cells in chronic lymphoid leukemia
authors: Porter DL, Levine BL, Kalos M, Bagg A, June CH
summary: Lentiviral CD19 CAR-T cells with 4-1BB costimulation expanded and induced complete remission in CLL.

title: Safety and tumor responses with lambrolizumab (anti-PD-1) in melanoma
authors: Hamid O, Robert C, Daud A, Hodi FS, Hwu WJ, Kefford R, et al.
summary: Early trial of lambrolizumab (pembrolizumab) showing high response rates, leading to the first anti-PD-1 approval (2014).

title: Chimeric antigen receptor T cells for sustained remissions in leukemia
authors: Maude SL, Frey N, Shaw PA, Aplenc R, Barrett DM, Bunin NJ, et al.
summary: CTL019 CAR-T achieved 90% complete remission in relapsed ALL, the basis for Kymriah approval.

title: Personalized RNA mutanome vaccines mobilize poly-specific therapeutic immunity against cancer
authors: Sahin U, Derhovanessian E, Miller M, Kloke BP, Simon P, Löwer M, et al.
summary: First-in-human individualized neoantigen mRNA vaccines in melanoma, establishing personalized cancer vaccines.

title: Approval of Kymriah (tisagenlecleucel), the first CAR-T cell therapy
authors: US Food and Drug Administration; Novartis
summary: First FDA-approved gene-modified cell therapy, for pediatric and young adult B-cell ALL.

title: Overall survival benefit with tebentafusp in metastatic uveal melanoma
authors: Nathan P, Hassel JC, Rutkowski P, Baurain JJ, Butler MO, Schlaak M, et al.
summary: First TCR-based bispecific (ImmTAC) to improve survival, validating soluble TCR therapeutics against intracellular antigens.

title: Anti-CD19 CAR T cell therapy for refractory systemic lupus erythematosus
authors: Mackensen A, Müller F, Mougiakakos D, Böltz S, Wilhelm A, Aigner M, et al.
summary: CD19 CAR-T induced drug-free remission in refractory lupus, extending CAR-T from cancer to autoimmune disease (followed by a 2024 NEJM case series).

title: GD2-CAR T cell therapy for diffuse midline gliomas
authors: Majzner RG, Ramakrishna S, Yeom KW, Patel S, Chinnasamy H, Schultz LM, et al.
summary: GD2-directed CAR-T cells produced responses in lethal pediatric gliomas, a step toward CAR-T for solid tumors.

title: Personalized RNA neoantigen vaccines stimulate T cells in pancreatic cancer
authors: Rojas LA, Sethna Z, Soares KC, Olcese C, Pang N, Patterson E, et al.
summary: Individualized mRNA neoantigen vaccines (autogene cevumeran) induced durable T cells correlated with delayed recurrence in pancreatic cancer.

title: Individualised neoantigen therapy mRNA-4157 (V940) plus pembrolizumab versus pembrolizumab monotherapy in resected melanoma (KEYNOTE-942): a randomised, phase 2b study
authors: Weber JS, Carlino MS, Khattak A, Meniawy T, Ansstas G, Taylor MH, et al.
summary: Randomized evidence that a personalized mRNA cancer vaccine added to anti-PD-1 reduces melanoma recurrence.

title: Diagnosis of Uterine Cancer by the Vaginal Smear
authors: Papanicolaou GN, Traut HF
summary: Established the Pap smear for cytological cancer screening, which greatly reduced cervical cancer mortality.

title: Immunoassay of endogenous plasma insulin in man
authors: Yalow RS, Berson SA
summary: Introduced radioimmunoassay for measuring hormones at picomolar concentrations (Nobel 1977).

title: A "new" antigen in leukemia sera
authors: Blumberg BS, Alter HJ, Visnich S
summary: Discovered the Australia antigen (HBsAg), enabling hepatitis B blood screening and later the hepatitis B vaccine.

title: Enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA). Quantitative assay of immunoglobulin G
authors: Engvall E, Perlmann P
summary: Invented ELISA, replacing radioisotopes with enzyme labels and becoming the most widely used immunodiagnostic format.

title: Clearblue One Step: first lateral-flow home pregnancy test
authors: Unilever
summary: Monoclonal-antibody lateral-flow immunoassay for hCG, popularizing the rapid test format later used for COVID-19 antigen tests.

title: Detection of specific polymerase chain reaction product by utilizing the 5'→3' exonuclease activity of Thermus aquaticus DNA polymerase
authors: Holland PM, Abramson RD, Watson R, Gelfand DH
summary: Introduced the 5' nuclease (TaqMan) probe principle for sequence-specific PCR detection.

title: Kinetic PCR analysis: real-time monitoring of DNA amplification reactions
authors: Higuchi R, Fockler C, Dollinger G, Watson R
summary: Real-time quantitative PCR via fluorescence monitoring, now the gold standard for molecular diagnostics.

title: Presence of fetal DNA in maternal plasma and serum
authors: Lo YMD, Corbetta N, Chamberlain PF, Rai V, Sargent IL, Redman CWG, et al.
summary: Discovered cell-free fetal DNA in maternal blood, the foundation of noninvasive prenatal testing and of cell-free DNA diagnostics.

title: Noninvasive prenatal diagnosis of fetal chromosomal aneuploidy by massively parallel genomic sequencing of DNA in maternal plasma
authors: Chiu RWK, Chan KCA, Gao Y, Lau VYM, Zheng W, Leung TY, et al.
summary: Counting sequencing reads from maternal plasma detected fetal trisomy 21, enabling clinical NIPT.

title: Detection of circulating tumor DNA in early- and late-stage human malignancies
authors: Bettegowda C, Sausen M, Leary RJ, Kinde I, Wang Y, Agrawal N, et al.
summary: Systematic survey of ctDNA across cancers showing liquid biopsy feasibility for detection and monitoring.

title: Nucleic acid detection with CRISPR-Cas13a/C2c2
